relations: Small surface ripples continuously break and re-form the vertical golden sun path while its position stays fixed.
Shallow water advancing and receding over right-side pebbles alternately dulls and brightens their glossy sheen.
The stationary crystal ball keeps its refracted upside-down horizon stable while its upper dark reflection shifts subtly.
Wet pebble sheen near the ball shifts gently as the thin water film moves across the stones.
caption: The video captures a low-angle sunset view over a calm body of water. A transparent crystal lens-ball sits on a bed of wet, dark pebbles in the left foreground. The ball refracts an upside-down image of the horizon and a bright sliver of the sun, while its upper surface holds a dark reflection that changes only subtly. The sun sits just above a distant flat shoreline, throwing a vertical golden glitter-path across the water, and the sky glows warm orange-pink with thin clouds. Throughout the view the framing remains nearly fixed, so most visible motion is in the water. Small ripples travel across the surface, continuously breaking and re-forming the sun's shimmering column so its shape and brightness fluctuate from moment to moment while its position remains the same. The sheen on the wet pebbles shifts subtly, and the shallow water line over the stones to the right of the ball appears to advance and recede, changing how glossy that area looks. The crystal ball itself neither rolls nor translates, and the viewpoint appears largely stable.
